resumen: One dumbbell held against the chest and a full squat. The weight up front keeps the trunk upright, which is why this is the one people learn the pattern with.
ejecucion: Hold a dumbbell against your chest with both hands, elbows tucked in.
Feet shoulder-width apart, toes turned slightly out.
Go down bending hips and knees together, knees tracking over your feet.
Go as low as you can keep your back flat: the weight in front helps you not tip forward.
Come up by pushing the floor away, keeping the dumbbell against your chest.
matices: Holding the load in front changes the demand compared with a back squat, but there is no settled answer on how much: it depends on load and depth, and activation studies mostly compare barbell variations.
